editorial: When the night’s lights flicker, you’re pulled into a game where fate writes its own chilling rules. Tarot (2024) marries traditional horror with a labyrinthine narrative that treats each card read as a breadcrumb into the abyss. The most striking moment is when Director Maya Li turns a single tarot spread into an immersive set, the cards glowing like trapped souls, and Catherine Keener gives a bone‑deep command of dread. Some may find the second act lurches slightly, climbing a wall too steep for the mid‑point pace. If you hunger for psychological suspense layered with folklore trickery, this film will keep you awake through the night.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
